senses.gloss: m. (μηλοπέπων) an apple-shaped melon, cucumber-melon, prob. the fruit squash (v. Sm. Ant. s. v.).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 1:2">Kil. I, 2</cite> <he>הקשות והמ׳ וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>הקישות והמלפפין</he>) cucumbers and melopepons are not forbidden as mingled seeds (<cite ref="K00674"><he>כִּלְאַיִם</he></cite>); <cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 2:6">Ter. II, 6</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:2:2">Y. Kil. I, 27ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>לפום כן … בלישנא יוני מ׳ …</he> (not <he>יונא</he>) therefore (because it is a hybrid product of apple [μῆλον] and pepon [σίκυα πέπων] they call it in Greek melopepon.
<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 5:3">Tosef. Shebi. V, 3</cite> (missing in ed. Zuck.) <he>עיקר המלפפין</he> (Var. <he>הבלבסין</he>) the real fruit melopepon (contrad. to leaves).
<cite ref="Tosefta Uktsin 2:10">Tosef. Ukts. II, 10</cite> <cite ref="M01610"><he>מלפין</he></cite> (Var. <he>טלפין</he>; corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 968:28">Yalk. Koh. 968</cite> <he>אפי׳ … מלפפונין וכ׳</he> even melopepons in Nisan were not absent from Solomon’s table; Tanḥ. Yithro 7 <cite ref="M01606"><he>מלספנון</he></cite>; ed. Bub. 5 <he>בילפפונין</he> (corr. acc.).
